stories.headline: China Condemns UK Nationalization of British Steel, Threatens to Defend Chinese Investors
stories.summary:
China's commerce ministry issued a sharp rebuke Friday over the UK government's decision to nationalize British Steel, saying the move "seriously infringed upon Jingye's legitimate rights and interests" and "severely undermined the confidence of Chinese companies investing in the UK." Beijing called on Britain to honor its obligations under the 1986 China-UK Bilateral Investment Treaty and said it would support Chinese firms in protecting their legal rights, without specifying what measures it might take.

The UK Parliament passed legislation Wednesday authorizing the government to bring the steel industry into public ownership when it meets a public interest test. On Thursday, the government formally took control of British Steel's Scunthorpe operations, which had been owned by China's Jingye Group and were losing more than £1 million per day. Officials said nationalization was necessary to protect thousands of jobs and preserve a "vital national capability," adding that negotiations with Jingye had failed to produce a deal representing value to taxpayers.

Jingye is seeking compensation for the takeover. The UK government said it will appoint an independent valuer in autumn to assess any compensation due — and that the figure could be nil. A UK government spokesperson said London "highly values" its relationship with China and remains open to Chinese investment, even as the dispute threatens to strain bilateral ties.

The diplomatic friction arrives at a sensitive moment: incoming Prime Minister Andy Burnham is set to enter Downing Street on Monday and will immediately face the question of how to manage relations with Beijing while navigating the economic and strategic demands of the nationalization.

stories.headline: DOJ Clears Federal Employees to Download TikTok on Government Devices After ByteDance Divestiture
stories.summary:
The Department of Justice's Office of Legal Counsel issued a memo concluding that federal employees may now download TikTok onto government devices, reversing a ban that had been in place under a 2022 law. The opinion, addressed to the deputy counsel to President Trump, found that a completed restructuring of TikTok's U.S. operations has eliminated the national security risks that originally prompted the prohibition.

The change follows ByteDance's transfer of control over TikTok's U.S. user data and operations to TikTok U.S. Data Security (TikTok USDS), a joint venture in which American and global investors hold 80.1% and ByteDance retains a 19.9% minority stake. The divestiture was required by a 2024 law signed by President Biden, which the Supreme Court unanimously upheld in January 2025. The DOJ concluded that ByteDance's minority shareholder status "makes no practical difference" to the platform's security posture.

The ruling represents a significant policy reversal on an issue that generated years of bipartisan concern in Congress. Critics of the original ban had argued it infringed on the free speech rights of TikTok's tens of millions of American users, while national security hawks worried about Chinese government access to U.S. data. The DOJ's opinion suggests the completed ownership restructuring has, in the administration's view, resolved those concerns.

Individual agencies retain discretion over whether to allow the app on their devices, consistent with their own workplace policies. The decision is likely to renew debate over whether the structural safeguards of the divestiture deal are sufficient, given ByteDance's continued minority ownership stake.

stories.headline: Indian Activist Sonam Wangchuk Forcibly Hospitalized After 20-Day Hunger Strike in Delhi
stories.summary:
Indian activist and educationist Sonam Wangchuk was removed from his protest site at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi early Saturday morning by dozens of police and paramilitary personnel and taken by ambulance to Safdarjung Hospital. The 59-year-old had been on an indefinite hunger strike for 20 days, consuming only salt and water, in support of the Cockroach Janta Party, a satirical online movement seeking educational reform. He had lost more than 9 kilograms and was reported to be in significant pain.

Authorities said the removal was carried out in compliance with a Delhi High Court order issued Thursday directing the federal government to monitor Wangchuk's health and provide treatment if necessary. Police officials described the move as medically motivated. Hospital superintendent Dr. Charu Bamba said Wangchuk was "fully alert and stable" but experiencing mild dehydration and weakness from prolonged fasting.

Videos from the scene showed chaotic scenes as protesters who attempted to block the removal were pushed aside by security forces, who covered Wangchuk with bedsheets before carrying him away. His wife, Gitanjali Angmo, posted on social media from the hospital asking that nothing be administered to him without consent from family and his monitoring physicians.

The protest group's founder, Abhijeet Dipke, announced he would begin an indefinite fast in Wangchuk's place and called for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to resign. He said a planned march to parliament on Monday would proceed. Wangchuk is widely known internationally for his work on sustainable development in the Ladakh region and as an inspiration for a character in the 2009 Bollywood film "3 Idiots."

stories.headline: Update: China's Open-Weight AI Push Threatens to Undercut U.S. Premium Models
stories.summary:
A strategic split is emerging in the global artificial intelligence race, with Chinese laboratories increasingly focusing on open-weight models — AI systems whose underlying parameters are publicly released — as a way to compete with, and potentially undercut, premium closed models from American companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Axios reports that companies were already shifting away from expensive U.S. AI products toward cheaper Chinese alternatives before Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 model drew significant attention for its performance and accessibility.

The strategic concern for Silicon Valley is that building the world's most capable models may no longer be sufficient to win the market if Chinese competitors can offer freely customizable, low-cost alternatives. Open-weight models allow businesses and developers to modify and deploy AI without paying per-query fees, making them attractive for cost-sensitive enterprise adoption globally — including in markets where U.S. firms have regulatory or geopolitical disadvantages.

The development intensifies an already fraught technology competition between Washington and Beijing. U.S. export controls on advanced semiconductors were intended in part to slow Chinese AI progress, but open-weight strategies allow Chinese labs to distribute influence even if their raw compute is constrained. The approach mirrors earlier dynamics in mobile software, where Android's open ecosystem ultimately achieved broader global reach than Apple's closed iOS platform.

Analysts note that the bifurcation poses a long-term commercial and national security challenge: if Chinese open-weight models become the default infrastructure for AI development in much of the world, U.S. firms risk being relegated to premium niches even if they retain a technical edge in top-tier model performance.

stories.headline: Update: Iran Seizes Ships in Strait of Hormuz as U.S. Blockade Intensifies, Ceasefire Collapses
stories.summary:
The U.S.-Iran conflict escalated sharply this week as Iranian forces seized two cargo ships in the Strait of Hormuz, including the Epaminondas, and declared the waterway closed. President Trump responded by reinstating a naval blockade of Iranian ports and announcing a 20% charge on all cargo transiting the strait, marking a significant expansion of economic and military pressure on Tehran.

U.S. strikes continued for a seventh consecutive night, targeting an Iranian submarine and ship maintenance facility. Iran retaliated by striking U.S. military assets and allies across the region, with Kuwait reporting that a power and water plant was hit by an Iranian drone. Attacks were also reported against U.S. positions in Jordan, Bahrain, and Oman.

Trump told reporters he had not yet decided whether to 'finish off' Iran, leaving open the question of whether the conflict could escalate to a broader ground or air campaign. Ceasefire negotiations have collapsed, and global energy markets have seen sharp swings, with UK fuel prices rising in the aftermath of the failed peace talks.

The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most critical oil shipping chokepoints, with roughly 20% of global petroleum passing through it. Iran's top negotiator asserted that Tehran 'will decide the right of passage,' directly challenging the U.S. blockade and raising fears of prolonged disruption to global energy supplies.

stories.headline: Russia Detains Ex-Putin Supporter Blogger, Bars Anti-War Politician from Election
stories.summary:
Russian authorities moved on Friday to further suppress domestic dissent, remanding blogger Ilya Remeslo in pre-trial detention for two months and barring opposition politician Boris Nadezhdin from collecting parliamentary election signatures. Remeslo, once a prominent pro-Kremlin voice, is accused of spreading false information about the military after a March 2026 blog post titled 'Five Reasons Why I Stopped Supporting Vladimir Putin,' in which he called the president a 'war criminal and thief.'

Nadezhdin, 63, a former MP who previously attempted an anti-war presidential run, was convicted of 'displaying extremist symbols' after reposting a video in 2023 that briefly showed an image of Alexei Navalny. The conviction bars him from gathering the signatures needed to register as a parliamentary candidate ahead of September elections. He was also declared a 'foreign agent' last week and barred from leaving the country.

Nadezhdin denied the charges in court, saying they were designed to silence him and prevent his candidacy. He noted all his accounts had been frozen, making it impossible to pay even the nominal fine of 1,000 roubles. He briefly collapsed during his court appearance, reportedly due to high blood pressure and diabetes.

The twin actions underscore the narrowing space for political opposition in Russia. Most genuine opposition figures have gone into exile, and Navalny, the country's most prominent opposition leader, died in an Arctic penal colony in February 2024 under circumstances that the UK and four European nations have attributed to poisoning.

stories.headline: Update: Taylor Farms Pulls Iceberg Lettuce Products Amid Growing Cyclosporiasis Outbreak
stories.summary:
California-based vegetable producer Taylor Farms announced Friday it will voluntarily remove all iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico after the FDA provided information linking the supply to a growing cyclosporiasis outbreak across the United States. The parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis, which causes intestinal illness, has been tied to multiple cases in recent weeks.

Taylor Farms stated that none of its branded salad kits contain the specific iceberg lettuce associated with the outbreak, but the precautionary removal applies to products sourced from its Taylor Farms de Mexico operation. The FDA has been investigating the supplier chain as part of its probe into the outbreak's source.

The development is a concrete new step in an ongoing food-safety investigation that has already prompted Taco Bell to remove lettuce from some of its locations. Cyclosporiasis infections typically cause prolonged diarrhea and gastrointestinal distress, with symptoms sometimes lasting weeks if untreated.

stories.headline: Paul Pelosi Charged with Misdemeanor Hit-and-Run in Napa County
stories.summary:
Paul Pelosi, 86, the husband of former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, was charged Friday with a misdemeanor hit-and-run after allegedly striking a parked, unoccupied car in Napa County and leaving the scene in early July. The Napa County District Attorney's office announced the charge under California law requiring drivers involved in property-damage collisions to stop and provide their information. The struck vehicle sustained what authorities described as 'major' damage.

The charge comes four years after Pelosi pleaded guilty to a DUI charge stemming from a 2022 car crash in which another driver was injured. Public records show Pelosi has a history of traffic infractions in California stretching back to at least 2011. Nancy Pelosi declined to answer reporters' questions about the case before a staffer ended the exchange.

The charge is a misdemeanor and carries no immediate national policy consequences, but the incident drew significant media attention given the family's political prominence and Paul Pelosi's prior criminal record involving driving offenses.
